questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of lǐfàde dìfang?
What is an independent barbershop called?
What is a COMPOUND VERB OF RESULT?
What two verbs make up kànjian, and what does each mean?
What is the literal meaning of xià lóu?
Which two kinds of compound verb have you now learned?

answers.answer_text: Compound verbs of direction (chūqu, chūlai — motion verb plus lái or qù) and compound verbs of result (kànjian — action verb plus a verb expressing the result).

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I looked but I didn't see."
How can kànjian be understood literally?

answers.answer_text: As "to look with the result of perceiving" — that is, "to see."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Did you hear her?"
Give the literal rendering of Kànjian dìyīge lùkǒu, wàng zuǒ guǎi.

answers.answer_text: "When you see the first intersection, turn left" — i.e. "Take your first left."

articles.text:
3. A: Qǐngwèn, nǐmen zhèli yǒu       May I ask, is there a place to get
      meiyou lǐfàde dìfang?           a haircut here?
   C: Yǒu. Cóng zhèli wàng zuǒ       Yes. From here you go to the left.
      zǒu. Xià lóu, jiù kànjian       Go downstairs, and then you'll
      le.                             see it.

4. A: Wǒ xiān cóng zhèli wàng zuǒ    From here I first go to the left.
      zǒu. Ránhòu xià lóutī jiù       After that, when I have gone down-
      kànjian le, shi bu shi?         stairs, I'll see it. Is that it?
   C: Shì.                            Yes.

Notes on Nos. 3-4

Lǐfàde dìfang means, literally, "a place where they cut hair." Note that lǐfà is also pronounced lǐfǎ. (An independent barbershop is called a lǐfàguǎn, "hair-cutting establishment.")

Xià lóu literally means "descend from an upper story." The English phrase "go/come downstairs" looks at the same action from another point of view: descend to a lower story.

The verb kànjian, "to see," is called a COMPOUND VERB OF RESULT. You have already learned about compound verbs made up of a verb indicating motion (such as chū, "to exit") followed by a verb indicating direction (lái or qù): chūqu, chūlai. Now you see, in exchanges 3 and 4, a compound verb made up of an action verb (kàn, "to look") and a verb expressing the result of that action (jiàn, "to perceive"). Kànjian can be understood as "to look with the result of perceiving," that is, "to see." Contrast kàn with kànjian:

Wǒ kànle kěshi méi kànjian.      I looked but I didn't see.

Here are other examples of compound verbs of result containing the verbs tīng, "to listen," and kàn:

Tā gēn ni shuō huà ne.           She is talking with you. Did you
Nǐ tīngjian le meiyou?           hear her?
Kànjian dìyīge lùkǒu, wàng       Take your first left. (literally,
zuǒ guǎi.                        "When you see the first intersec-
                                 tion, turn left.")
